question: In T lymphocytes, which of the following molecules has co-stimulatory activity ?:
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: LFA-1 -> interacts with ICAM-1 -> provides co-stimulatory activity -> 80% CHAIN: B7-1 -> binds to CD28 on T cells -> delivers co-stimulatory signals -> 80%
enhanced_information: In T lymphocytes, the molecule B7-1 provides co-stimulatory activity by binding to CD28 on T cells. This interaction delivers co-stimulatory signals. Evidence supports the interaction of LFA-1 with ICAM-1, but this pathway does not directly relate to co-stimulatory activity in this context.
analysis: In T lymphocytes, the molecule B7-1 is known to provide co-stimulatory activity by binding to CD28 on T cells. This interaction delivers essential co-stimulatory signals. While LFA-1 does interact with ICAM-1, this pathway is not directly related to co-stimulatory activity in this context. Therefore, the most likely correct option for co-stimulatory activity in T lymphocytes is B7-1.
